answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity with a graduated bond that vests only after a delay. Each new agent must lock a scarce credential whose required amount scales with how many identities share its funding source, and the deposit stays frozen while history is scored, so a fresh identity sits at a vertex of zero trust and inherits no reputation. To mint a thousand fakes the attacker must post a thousand separate locks and tie up that capital for months, while honest agents reclaim the bond later. Credentials also publish an umber digest and draw from a shared prism of randomness.
